faqs.a:
Temporary charges are hereby adopted to encourage water customers to use less water
               during the drought. The drought surcharge is calculated on the basis of how much water
               a customer uses and any resulting charge is in addition to the charge derived from
               water user rates as set forth in
sections 102-170
,
102-171
,
102-172
and
102-173
. The bimonthly water surcharge shall be calculated from the following rate structure:
(1)
Single-family or other individually connected units:
a.
0 to 12,000 gallons at the rate of $0.00 per 1,000 gallons.
b.
12,001 to 30,000 gallons at the rate of $0.30 per 1,000 gallons.
c.
30,001 to 60,000 gallons at the rate of $0.60 per 1,000 gallons.
d.
60,001 to 90,000 gallons at the rate of $0.90 per 1,000 gallons.
e.
Over 90,000 gallons at the rate of $1.20 per 1,000 gallons.
(2)
Duplex, multifamily, townhouse, or other units that are interconnected:
a.
0 to 12,000 gallons for the first unit plus 6,000 gallons for each additional unit
                  at the rate of $0.00 per 1,000 gallons.
b.
18,001 to 30,000 gallons for the first unit plus 13,000 gallons for each additional
                  unit at the rate of $0.30 per 1,000 gallons.
c.
30,001 to 60,000 gallons for the first unit plus 26,000 gallons for each additional
                  unit at the rate of $0.60 per 1,000 gallons.
d.
60,001 to 90,000 gallons for the first unit plus 39,000 gallons for each additional
                  unit at the rate of $0.90 per 1,000 gallons.
e.
All remaining usage at the rate of $1.20 per 1,000 gallons.
(3)
Nonresidential accounts except irrigation only:

(4)

All irrigation only accounts will have a surcharge of $1.20 per 1,000 gallons.
(
Ord. No. 4385, § 1, 5-20-2013
)
Note—
Section 2 of Ord. No. 4385
states: "The intent of the City Council is that the surcharges set forth herein are
               temporary and imposed only for the duration of the drought, such duration to be based
               on the determination of drought made by the Denver Water Board. At such time as the
               Denver Water Board rescinds the drought surcharges they have imposed on Denver customers,
               the Arvada City Council will rescind the drought surcharges that are the subject of
               this ordinance. Until rescinded as provided herein, the surcharges shall remain in
               effect."
Note—
Section 3 of Ord. No. 4385
states: "The surcharge rates set forth herein shall take effect on a date that is
               the latter of June 1, 2013 or such later date set by the Denver Water Board for the
               implementation of surcharge fees and rates during calendar year 2013."
